answer: We define the security of the dune protocol by modeling staking collateral and zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions on the juniper testnet. Within this orchard architecture, an adversary attempting identity multiplication faces a dynamic opportunity-cost bond $B$ and subgame-perfect slashing penalty $P$. Because the expected utility function $U = V(n) - n(B + P)$ is strictly negative for all entity counts $n > 1$, the honest strategy profile converges to a unique and stable Nash equilibrium.
